user.title: FindMyApple
user.description: What do you want to track?

menu_options.tags: AirTags and other Find My tags (experimental)

select_devices.title: Choose devices
select_devices.description: Select the devices to track. Each one gets a map tracker and sensors. Every update asks the selected devices for a fresh location, which uses a little battery.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again
reauth_confirm.description: Apple ended the session for {username}. Enter the password to sign in again.

icloud.title: Sign in with your Apple Account
icloud.description: Uses the same iCloud web service as icloud.com/find. If Advanced Data Protection is on, enable "Access iCloud Data on the Web" on your iPhone first.

data_description.remember_password: Lets Home Assistant sign in again on its own when Apple ends the session. The password is stored unencrypted in Home Assistant's .storage folder (and in backups). If off, you'll be asked to sign in again when the session expires (about every 2 months).

tags.title: Find My tags: sign in
tags.description: Experimental. To read tag locations, Home Assistant signs in as an emulated Mac: it downloads Apple's macOS ADI library from Apple (about 3.5 MB) and adds one "MacBook Pro" with a serial starting with 0FMAHA to your Apple Account's device list. Your password is stored unencrypted in Home Assistant's .storage folder, because Apple's session renewal needs it.

tags_2fa_method.title: Two-factor authentication
tags_2fa_method.description: Where should Apple send the code?

tags_unlock.title: Unlock your tag keys
tags_unlock.description: Your tags' keys are stored in your iCloud Keychain. Choose one of your Apple devices and enter its screen passcode (iPhone PIN or Mac login password, not your Apple Account password). It's used once and never stored. Apple locks keychain recovery after repeated wrong passcodes; attempts left here: {attempts_left}.

tags_select.title: Choose tags
tags_select.description: Select the tags to track. iPhones and other Apple devices are listed too, but the iCloud option tracks them better.

error.invalid_auth: Apple refused the email or password.
error.invalid_code: The code was not accepted. Check it and try again.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach iCloud, or Apple is temporarily refusing sign-ins. Wait a few minutes and try again.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. See the log for details.
error.machine_failed: Could not prepare the emulated Mac (downloading Apple's library or registering with Apple failed). See the log.

abort.already_configured: This Apple Account is already set up.
abort.security_key_unsupported: This account uses a hardware security key for two-factor authentication, which isn't supported yet.
abort.not_activated: Find My isn't available on iCloud.com for this account. With Advanced Data Protection on, enable "Access iCloud Data on the Web" (Settings → your name → iCloud) and try again.
abort.no_devices: No Find My devices were found on this account.
abort.cannot_connect: Signed in, but the device list could not be loaded. Try again in a few minutes.
abort.no_findmy_token: Signed in, but Apple didn't issue the Find My token. Try again later.
abort.no_escrow: No Apple device with a recoverable iCloud Keychain was found on this account.
abort.too_many_passcode_attempts: Too many wrong passcodes. Stopped to protect your account from a keychain lockout.
abort.no_tags: No Find My tags were found on this account.

data_description.away_min_interval: Used right outside a zone. The interval grows with distance up to the longest one (reached 50 km from the nearest zone). Each update makes the devices fetch a GPS position.

error.min_above_max: The shortest interval must not be longer than the longest one.
